conventions.convention: Assume Countable Choice; H is a nonzero complex Hilbert space with inner product linear in its first argument and adjoint defined by ⟨Mx,y⟩=⟨x,M*y⟩.
There are m≥1 outcomes, each with q_a≥0 bounded Kraus operators. Empty inner sums are zero; normalization is Σ_{a,r} M*_{a,r}M_{a,r}=I_H.
A density operator is self-adjoint, positive and trace class with trace one. The conditional update is defined only when its outcome probability is positive.

Formal series are coefficient sequences indexed by n≥0, with finite Cauchy products. Numerical evaluation uses g^0=1 even at zero; 0!=1. The convergence radius is the supremum in [0,+∞] of radii on whose open disks every evaluation converges.

load_bearing.statement: Under Countable Choice, for a normalized finite bounded Kraus instrument on H and a density operator ρ, every E_a is an effect and every J_a(ρ) is positive trace class; p_a=tr(J_a(ρ))=tr(ρE_a)∈[0,1] and Σ_a p_a=1. The nonselective output is a density operator; J_a(ρ)/p_a is a density operator when p_a>0, and the normalized update is undefined when p_a=0. For unit ψ and ρ=T_{ψ,ψ}, p_a=Σ_r‖M_{a,r}ψ‖².

Under Countable Choice, a finite bounded Kraus instrument datum on a nonzero complex Hilbert space H consists of m≥1, integers q_a≥0, and M_{a,r}∈B(H). It is normalized when Σ_{a,r}M*_{a,r}M_{a,r}=I_H. Define E_a=Σ_rM*_{a,r}M_{a,r} and J_a(X)=Σ_rM_{a,r}XM*_{a,r} for X∈B(H), with empty sums zero.
The coefficient sequence (n!)_{n≥0} defines a formal complex series whose numerical series converges at g=0 and diverges at every nonzero complex g, so its numerical convergence radius is zero.

published_dependencies.used_for: Exact AC_ω hypothesis for adjoints, trace-class calculus and density expansions.
Cauchy-sequence completeness of the underlying complex inner-product space.
First-argument linearity, conjugate symmetry and induced norm.
The space B(H) and its pointwise vector operations.
The inequality ‖Mx‖≤‖M‖‖x‖ used in finite-operation estimates.
The defining adjoint identity under Countable Choice.
Boundedness of adjoints, equality of adjoint norms and M**=M.
Separate definitions of self-adjointness and positivity.
Trace class and trace norm through summable singular values.
Trace relative to a supplied Hilbert basis; ambient basis existence is not assumed.
Basis-free nuclear trace, linearity and |tr(T)|≤‖T‖₁, giving trace-norm continuity.
Trace-class closure under bounded multiplication, finite sums and the sandwich estimate.
Rank-one positivity, trace and trace norm, and bounded left/right multiplication identities.
Trace cyclicity with bounded factors, retaining absolute convergence and trace-norm convergence.
Clause (a): density operators and their finite or countable orthonormal expansions in trace norm under Countable Choice. Clause (c), which additionally assumes full Choice, is not used.
